Answer: C
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 1b) clearly shows a large mass located in the posterior aspect of the thorax, compressing the lung tissue anteriorly. The frontal view (Figure 1a) demonstrates near-complete opacification of the right hemithorax with preservation of the tracheal midline position and lack of significant cardiac displacement to the left, which is characteristic of a large posterior mediastinal mass (such as a neurogenic tumor) that pushes the lung forward rather than shifting the mediastinum contralaterally like an anterior mass or massive effusion would.
